questions.q: A 28-year-old patient presents with persistent pink-red macules at healed acne sites. Dermoscopy shows telangiectatic vessels (post-inflammatory erythema, PIE). The most appropriate laser to selectively target the chromophore in this lesion is:
opts: 585–595nm pulsed dye laser (PDL)
755nm alexandrite laser
1064nm Nd:YAG laser
2940nm Er:YAG laser
questions.exp: PIE is caused by persistent dilated blood vessels; the chromophore is oxyhemoglobin (peak absorption ~542 and 577nm). The 585–595nm PDL selectively targets oxyhemoglobin via selective photothermolysis. Alexandrite targets melanin, long-pulsed Nd:YAG targets deeper vessels, and Er:YAG is an ablative resurfacing laser with no vascular selectivity.

questions.q: When reconstituting 100-unit vials of botulinum toxin type A with bacteriostatic 0.9% NaCl (containing benzyl alcohol) rather than non-preserved saline, which of the following is CORRECT?
opts: Increases risk of neutralising antibody formation against the toxin
Reduces injection-associated pain due to benzyl alcohol's mild local anaesthetic properties
Shortens duration of effect by accelerating toxin degradation
Is contraindicated as benzyl alcohol irreversibly denatures the toxin protein
questions.exp: Benzyl alcohol, the preservative in bacteriostatic saline, acts as a mild local anaesthetic, reducing the sting on injection — a well-documented clinical advantage. Studies show no significant increase in antibody formation or meaningful reduction in efficacy duration. Bacteriostatic saline does not denature the toxin at standard dilution volumes.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops firm, non-fluctuant subcutaneous nodules 18 months after hyaluronic acid filler injection. Aspiration yields no fluid. The MOST appropriate first-line treatment is:
opts: Hyaluronidase injection into the nodules
Intralesional 5-fluorouracil (50 mg/mL) monotherapy
Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide combined with 5-fluorouracil
Surgical excision under local anaesthesia
questions.exp: Late, non-fluctuant nodules appearing >6 months post-HA filler represent biofilm-associated or foreign body granulomas, not simple filler nodules. Hyaluronidase is ineffective against established granulomas. Intralesional triamcinolone (10–20 mg/mL) + 5-FU (50 mg/mL) combination is first-line, reducing fibrosis through complementary mechanisms (corticosteroid inhibits fibroblast activity; 5-FU inhibits fibroblast proliferation).

questions.q: Diphencyprone (DPCP) is used as a contact sensitiser in alopecia areata. Its mechanism of action promoting hair regrowth is BEST described as:
opts: Direct cytotoxic effect on autoreactive CD8+ T cells within the peribulbar infiltrate
Upregulation of IL-10 secretion by regulatory T cells, globally suppressing autoimmunity
Competitive inhibition of NKG2D receptor on perifollicular NK cells
Hapten-induced antigenic competition diverting the immune response away from follicular antigens
questions.exp: DPCP functions as a hapten creating contact hypersensitivity. The leading mechanistic hypothesis is 'antigenic competition' — the robust hapten-specific Th1 response diverts autoreactive T cells away from follicular MICA antigens (normally recognised by NKG2D+ NK/NKT cells). This immune privilege shift in the follicular microenvironment allows melanocyte and follicular stem cell recovery. DPCP does not act primarily via IL-10 or direct T-cell cytotoxicity.

questions.q: For L-ascorbic acid to penetrate the stratum corneum efficiently AND remain chemically stable in a topical formulation, the optimal formulation parameters are:
opts: pH ≤3.5 and concentration ≥10%
pH 5.0–6.0 and concentration ≥5%
pH ≤3.5 and concentration <5%
pH 7.0 and concentration ≥20%
questions.exp: L-ascorbic acid has a pKa of 4.2; at pH ≤3.5, it remains fully protonated (neutral charge), maximising lipid solubility and stratum corneum penetration. Concentrations below 10% produce minimal biological effect; therapeutic range is 10–20%. At neutral or alkaline pH, ascorbic acid rapidly oxidises to dehydroascorbic acid, losing both stability and efficacy.

questions.q: A patient is concerned about oxybenzone in sunscreen during pregnancy. The primary evidence-based safety concern regarding oxybenzone relates to:
opts: Direct UV-induced photoallergy causing systemic anaphylactic reactions
Endocrine-disrupting potential via oestrogen receptor agonism detected in animal and in vitro studies
Nephrotoxicity due to percutaneous accumulation in renal tubular cells
Photodegradation producing reactive oxygen species within the dermis
questions.exp: Oxybenzone (benzophenone-3) is a chemical UVB/UVA-II filter with significant percutaneous absorption — detected in blood, urine, and breast milk. Animal and in vitro studies demonstrate weak oestrogenic activity via oestrogen receptor binding (endocrine disruption). This is the primary concern in pregnancy and in children. It does not cause nephrotoxicity or clinically significant photoallergy at sunscreen concentrations.

questions.q: During a TCA peel, the endpoint observed is erythema with scattered streaks of white frosting but with the pink background still clearly visible (Level I frosting). This appearance indicates the peel has penetrated to the depth of:
opts: Stratum granulosum only (very superficial)
Papillary dermis
Full-thickness epidermal penetration (epidermis only)
Mid-reticular dermis
questions.exp: TCA frosting levels indicate depth: Level I (erythema with streaks of white frost, pink background visible) = full-thickness epidermis; Level II (white coating with erythema visible through frost) = papillary dermis; Level III (solid, opaque white frost with no erythema) = upper reticular dermis. Level I represents epidermal coagulation without dermal penetration, equivalent to a superficial-to-medium transition peel.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman undergoes 810nm diode laser hair removal for facial hair. After 4 sessions, she notices increased, thicker dark hair in the treated area extending beyond the original treatment zone. The MOST likely explanation for this paradoxical hypertrichosis is:
opts: Laser-induced heat-shock protein upregulation activating dormant telogen follicles throughout the scalp
Increased local DHT sensitivity in follicles that received subthreshold laser fluence
MSH surge post-laser causing melanogenesis and hypertrophy in surrounding follicles
Subthreshold photothermal energy at treatment margins stimulating rather than destroying follicles, activating stem cells
questions.exp: Paradoxical hypertrichosis results from subthreshold (insufficient to destroy) laser energy stimulating the hair follicle — analogous to low-level laser therapy promoting growth. Follicles at the periphery of the treatment zone receive fluences below the destruction threshold but sufficient for thermal stimulation of stem cells in the bulge region. Risk is higher in Fitzpatrick types III–V, hormonal skin (upper lip, jaw), and in patients with polycystic ovarian syndrome.

questions.q: For PRP activation to achieve physiological release of growth factors from alpha granules, the activating combination that MOST closely mimics in vivo wound healing is:
opts: Calcium chloride (CaCl₂) combined with autologous thrombin
Freeze-thaw cycling at −20°C for 30 minutes
Bovine collagen matrix added to the PRP prior to injection
Sonication at 40 kHz for 30 seconds
questions.exp: In vivo platelet activation occurs through the coagulation cascade: thrombin cleaves fibrinogen to fibrin, and calcium reverses anticoagulation. Adding exogenous CaCl₂ (10%, 50–70 µL per mL PRP) to autologous thrombin most faithfully replicates this, triggering release of PDGF, TGF-β1, VEGF, and EGF from alpha granules. Bovine thrombin carries alloimmunisation risk; freeze-thaw and sonication are non-physiological and may denature growth factors.

questions.q: Topical tacrolimus 0.1% is used as a steroid-sparing agent in vitiligo. Its principal mechanism enabling repigmentation is:
opts: Direct stimulation of melanocyte proliferation via c-Kit/SCF receptor activation
Inhibition of T-cell apoptosis in the perifollicular region, preserving the melanocyte reservoir
Calcineurin inhibition preventing IL-2 transcription and suppressing CD8+ T-cell–mediated melanocyte destruction
Upregulation of stem cell factor (SCF) in keratinocytes adjacent to the depigmented zone
questions.exp: Vitiligo pathogenesis involves CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell activation via the calcineurin-NFAT pathway, leading to IFN-γ and CXCL10 secretion and targeted melanocyte destruction. Tacrolimus (FK506) binds FKBP12, inhibiting calcineurin and blocking NFAT nuclear translocation, preventing IL-2 gene transcription and CD8+ T-cell activation. This immunosuppression allows melanocyte precursors in the hair follicle bulge to migrate and repopulate the epidermis.

questions.q: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is increasingly used in preference to PRP for hair restoration and skin rejuvenation. The MOST clinically relevant advantage of PRF over conventional PRP is:
opts: Higher platelet concentration (5–7× baseline) compared to PRP (2–3× baseline)
Absence of leukocytes, producing a non-inflammatory, purely regenerative preparation
Compatibility with heterologous donor blood due to the universal fibrin scaffold
Slow, sustained release of growth factors over 7–14 days from the 3D fibrin scaffold
questions.exp: PRF is prepared without anticoagulants, producing a fibrin matrix that traps platelets and leukocytes. This 3D scaffold releases PDGF, TGF-β1, VEGF, and IGF-1 slowly over 7–14 days — contrasting with PRP's rapid bolus release. PRF platelet concentration is not necessarily superior to PRP; it contains leukocytes (i-PRF is leukocyte-rich); and only autologous blood is used, making heterologous compatibility irrelevant.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with diffuse crown thinning with a preserved frontal hairline. Ludwig Grade II female pattern hair loss (FPHL) is characterised by:
opts: Minimal widening of the central part line, detectable only on close clinical inspection
Pronounced widening of the central part line with appreciable diffuse thinning of the crown
Complete baldness of the crown with only a peripheral rim of hair remaining
Bitemporal recession with relative preservation of the mid-scalp
questions.exp: Ludwig classification: Grade I — minimal widening of the central part, visible only on close inspection; Grade II — pronounced widening with clearly appreciable diffuse thinning over the crown; Grade III — extensive diffuse thinning throughout the top of the scalp with only a narrow peripheral rim of hair. Bitemporal recession is a feature of Hamilton-Norwood classification (male pattern) and is not characteristic of Ludwig FPHL.

questions.q: Magnesium ascorbyl phosphate (MAP) and ascorbyl-2-glucoside (AA2G) are stable vitamin C derivatives at neutral pH. The key difference in their cutaneous bioconversion is:
opts: MAP is dephosphorylated by cutaneous phosphatases; AA2G is hydrolysed by α-glucosidase (glucoamylase) to release L-ascorbic acid
Both derivatives require cytochrome P450 enzymes in the stratum spinosum for bioconversion
AA2G requires no enzymatic conversion; MAP requires UV exposure to release active ascorbic acid
MAP is biologically active as-is and requires no enzymatic conversion in skin
questions.exp: Both MAP and AA2G are prodrug derivatives that require enzymatic hydrolysis in the skin to release free L-ascorbic acid. MAP is cleaved by cutaneous phosphatase enzymes (alkaline/acid phosphatases present in the epidermis). AA2G (ascorbyl-2-glucoside) is hydrolysed by α-glucosidase (glucoamylase) activity. Both offer superior stability over L-ascorbic acid in formulations but require different enzymatic pathways for activation.

questions.q: Using the Kirby-Desai scale for predicting laser tattoo removal sessions, which colour of tattoo ink is MOST resistant to standard Q-switched Nd:YAG laser and would score the maximum on the colour parameter?
opts: Black — absorbs all wavelengths, making thermal diffusion unpredictable
Red — requires the 532nm wavelength, which is less commonly available
Green and yellow fluorescent — lacking an optimal wavelength in standard Q-switched device portfolios
Dark blue — poorly absorbed by 1064nm Nd:YAG due to spectral mismatch
questions.exp: In the Kirby-Desai scale, ink colour significantly predicts required sessions. Black ink absorbs 1064nm efficiently and scores 1 (easiest). Red responds to 532nm (score 2). Green and yellow fluorescent pigments are the most resistant — standard Q-switched 1064nm and 532nm Nd:YAG devices have poor absorption spectra for these colours; they score highest (most sessions predicted). Picosecond lasers with 730nm and 785nm outputs improve efficacy for these pigments.

questions.q: Injectable phosphatidylcholine (PC) preparations (e.g., Lipostabil) used for mesotherapy-based lipolysis exert their adipocytolytic effect primarily via:
opts: Phosphatidylcholine itself by activating endogenous adipocyte lipase enzymes
Lysophosphatidylcholine formed after phospholipase A2 digestion of the injected PC
Choline released from PC metabolism activating β3-adrenoceptors on adipocytes
Sodium deoxycholate (a bile salt detergent co-formulated with PC) disrupting adipocyte cell membranes
questions.exp: Commercial PC formulations contain sodium deoxycholate as a solubiliser. Research demonstrates that deoxycholate alone replicates the lipolytic and adipocytolytic effect of the PC formulation — it acts as a detergent, disrupting the adipocyte plasma membrane. Pure PC without deoxycholate has minimal in vivo lipolytic activity. ATX-101 (Kybella/Belkyra) — FDA-approved deoxycholic acid — confirmed this, with deoxycholate as the sole active ingredient.

questions.q: Compared to monopolar radiofrequency (RF), bipolar RF in skin tightening:
opts: Has shallower depth of penetration, as current flows between two closely spaced electrodes on the same handpiece
Requires a grounding pad placed on the patient's back to complete the electrical circuit
Achieves greater depth of penetration because the circuit closes through the patient's body
Produces identical depth to monopolar RF at equivalent frequency and power settings
questions.exp: In bipolar RF, current flows between two electrodes positioned on the same handpiece. Penetration depth equals approximately half the inter-electrode distance (typically 2–4mm — targeting the dermis). Monopolar RF uses one active electrode with a remote grounding pad on the body, directing current through deeper tissues (4–6mm or beyond, reaching the SMAS). The grounding pad requirement distinguishes monopolar from bipolar; no pad = bipolar.

questions.q: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) for facial lifting is absolutely contraindicated in patients with:
opts: Fitzpatrick skin types V–VI with significant baseline epidermal melanin
Active implanted electronic devices (pacemaker, neurostimulator) in or near the treatment field
Prior botulinum toxin injection within the preceding 3 months
Stable thyroid disease managed with levothyroxine monotherapy
questions.exp: HIFU delivers focused mechanical and thermal energy deep in tissue. Active implanted electronic devices (cardiac pacemakers, neurostimulators, cochlear implants) within or near the treatment field are an absolute contraindication — HIFU energy can cause electromagnetic interference, device malfunction, or thermal injury at the device-tissue interface. Fitzpatrick type, recent Botox, and stable thyroid medication are not absolute contraindications; the thyroid area itself should be avoided as a treatment zone.

questions.q: During FUE hair transplant harvesting from a patient with fine, straight hair and low donor density, the punch choice that MINIMISES transection rate is:
opts: Sharp straight-edged punch (0.9mm) with slow unidirectional drill rotation
Blunt punch (1.0mm) with oscillating motion to avoid follicular winding
Sharp serrated (flared/trumpet) punch (0.8mm) with oscillating or hybrid rotation
Motorised straight trumpet punch (1.2mm) at high speed for efficiency
questions.exp: Fine hair follicles have delicate shafts, shallower angles, and tighter curl patterns requiring precision. A sharp serrated (trumpet/flared) punch at 0.8mm with oscillating or hybrid (oscillation + rotation) motion cuts cleanly through the epidermis while oscillation prevents follicular winding — reducing transection significantly compared to unidirectional rotation. Larger punches (1.0–1.2mm) increase donor scarring and reduce graft yield per cm².

questions.q: A researcher studying UV carcinogenesis compares the DNA damage mechanisms of UVA and UVB. Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes their primary mechanisms?
opts: UVB directly forms cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) and 6-4 photoproducts; UVA primarily causes oxidative DNA damage via reactive oxygen species (ROS)
UVA directly forms CPDs via direct photon absorption; UVB causes indirect damage through hydrogen peroxide production
Both UVA and UVB form CPDs through identical direct photochemical mechanisms in epidermal DNA
UVB primarily causes DNA strand breaks; UVA exclusively induces point mutations via CPD formation
questions.exp: UVB (280–315nm) is directly absorbed by DNA pyrimidine bases, producing covalent photoproducts — cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) and 6-4 photoproducts between adjacent thymidines. UVA (315–400nm), though poorly absorbed by DNA directly, generates reactive oxygen species (singlet oxygen, superoxide, hydrogen peroxide) that cause indirect oxidative DNA damage, primarily 8-oxoguanine lesions — distinct from UVB's direct photoproducts and leading to different mutation signatures.

questions.q: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl) is a signal peptide used in anti-ageing cosmeceuticals. Its mechanism of action is:
opts: Directly inhibiting MMP-1 by competitive chelation of the active site zinc ion
Acting as a retinoid receptor agonist, upregulating RAR-β to increase procollagen transcription
Mimicking laminin-5 to stimulate keratinocyte proliferation at the dermoepidermal junction
Mimicking a collagen type I breakdown fragment (KTTKS), signalling fibroblasts to upregulate procollagen I, III, and fibronectin synthesis
questions.exp: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 consists of the sequence Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser (KTTKS) — a fragment generated during collagen type I degradation by MMPs — attached to palmitic acid for enhanced skin penetration. Fibroblasts 'interpret' this peptide as a signal of extracellular matrix breakdown and upregulate synthesis of procollagen I, III, and fibronectin. It does not directly inhibit MMPs, activate retinoid receptors, or stimulate keratinocytes.

questions.q: Pyruvic acid is an alpha-keto acid used as a superficial-to-medium chemical peeling agent. Its key advantage over glycolic acid for acne-prone, oily skin is:
opts: Greater keratolytic potency at lower concentrations due to its smaller molecular weight compared to glycolic acid
Triple action: keratolytic, antimicrobial (inhibits P. acnes metabolism), and sebostatic — ideal for acne-prone oily skin
Ability to penetrate to the reticular dermis at 50% concentration for deep collagen remodelling
Lower post-peel PIH risk due to a pH-independent, non-inflammatory mechanism of keratolysis
questions.exp: Pyruvic acid (an alpha-keto acid) has three distinct mechanisms: (1) keratolytic — disrupts corneocyte cohesion; (2) antimicrobial — inhibits bacterial metabolic enzymes (particularly P. acnes); (3) sebostatic — reduces sebaceous gland secretion. This triple action makes it superior to glycolic acid for inflammatory acne with oily skin. At 50% concentration, pyruvic acid achieves medium depth but does not reach the reticular dermis; phenol-croton oil combinations are required for deep peels.

questions.q: Following foam sclerotherapy for great saphenous vein (GSV) reflux in a 42-year-old woman, the recommended post-procedure compression regimen per European guidelines is:
opts: Class I compression stockings (15–21 mmHg) for 24 hours only, then none
Non-graded elastic bandage applied circumferentially for 48 hours
Class II medical compression stockings (23–32 mmHg) worn for 2–6 weeks
Class III compression (34–46 mmHg) for 1 week followed by Class II for 4 weeks
questions.exp: European Sclerotherapy Guidelines recommend Class II medical graduated compression (23–32 mmHg) for 2–6 weeks following foam sclerotherapy of the GSV. This maintains vein wall coaptation, prevents recanalisation of thrombus, and improves fibrotic obliteration rates. Class I compression is insufficient for large-vessel sclerotherapy. Class III stockings are typically reserved for severe chronic venous disease or lymphoedema, not routine post-sclerotherapy use.

questions.q: Acetyl hexapeptide-3 (Argireline) is marketed as a topical alternative to botulinum toxin. Its proposed mechanism of action is:
opts: Competing with SNAP-25 for SNARE complex assembly, partially inhibiting acetylcholine vesicle docking and fusion
Blocking muscarinic acetylcholine receptors post-synaptically at the neuromuscular junction
Inhibiting choline acetyltransferase, reducing acetylcholine synthesis in presynaptic terminals
Cleaving VAMP (synaptobrevin) at the presynaptic membrane, mimicking the action of BoNT-B
questions.exp: Argireline (Ac-EEMQRR-NH₂) is a hexapeptide fragment based on the N-terminal domain of SNAP-25. It competitively interferes with SNARE complex formation (the tripartite interaction of SNAP-25, syntaxin-1, and VAMP), partially inhibiting acetylcholine vesicle docking and exocytosis. Unlike botulinum toxin, Argireline does not cleave SNARE proteins and produces reversible, milder effects. Significant topical penetration to the neuromuscular junction remains debated.

questions.q: A paediatric dermatologist advises initiating pulsed dye laser (PDL) treatment for a port-wine stain (PWS) in a 2-year-old child rather than waiting for adulthood. The PRIMARY physiological rationale for early treatment is:
opts: Neonatal skin has higher dermal collagen content, making laser-induced thermocoagulation more efficient
Fewer epidermal melanocytes in infancy reduce competitive melanin absorption of the PDL wavelength
Adult PWS vessels migrate below the effective PDL penetration depth of 1–2mm
Infant PWS vessels are smaller in diameter, requiring less energy for thermocoagulation before progressive vascular ectasia develops
questions.exp: PWS vessels undergo progressive ectasia with age — childhood vessel diameters range from 10–50µm, expanding to 100–300µm in adult PWS. Smaller vessel diameters in infancy match the thermal relaxation time (TRT) for PDL settings more precisely, enabling efficient thermocoagulation with lower fluences. Early treatment prevents the progression to nodularity, tissue hypertrophy, and associated complications including Sturge-Weber syndrome involvement.

questions.q: Terbinafine's antifungal mechanism in dermatophyte infections specifically involves:
opts: Binding directly to ergosterol in the fungal membrane, forming ion channels causing cytoplasmic leakage
Inhibiting fungal squalene epoxidase (squalene monooxygenase), blocking ergosterol synthesis and causing toxic squalene accumulation
Inhibiting lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51), preventing lanosterol-to-ergosterol conversion in the fungal cell
Inhibiting β-1,3-glucan synthase, disrupting polysaccharide synthesis in the fungal cell wall
questions.exp: Terbinafine is an allylamine that specifically and non-competitively inhibits fungal squalene epoxidase, blocking the conversion of squalene to squalene-2,3-epoxide — an early step in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway. This causes dual fungal toxicity: ergosterol depletion AND intracellular squalene accumulation (directly toxic). Option A describes polyenes (amphotericin B, nystatin); option C describes azoles (fluconazole, itraconazole); option D describes echinocandins (caspofungin).

questions.q: During nail surgery, damage to which structure causes permanent nail dystrophy? The germinal matrix — responsible for 80–90% of nail plate production — is anatomically located:
opts: Visible as the lunula beneath the proximal nail fold — representing the distal extent of the germinal matrix
Distal to the lunula within the nail bed (sterile/distal matrix), producing the ventral nail plate layers
Proximal to the lunula, beneath the proximal nail fold — extending from the nail root to the proximal border of the lunula
In the hyponychium, distal to the free edge of the nail plate
questions.exp: The germinal (proximal) matrix extends from the nail root deep beneath the proximal nail fold to the proximal border of the lunula. It is responsible for 80–90% of nail plate production. The lunula (the white crescent) is actually the visible distal portion of the germinal matrix. The sterile (distal) matrix — the nail bed distal to the lunula — contributes the remaining 10–20% of nail plate thickness. Damage during proximal nail fold surgery or avulsion causes permanent dystrophy.

questions.q: For treating post-acne hyperpigmentation (PIH) in Fitzpatrick skin types IV–V using a superficial chemical peel, salicylic acid (SA) is preferred over glycolic acid (GA) primarily because:
opts: SA has a lower pKa than GA, conferring greater keratolytic potency at equivalent molar concentrations
SA penetrates to the reticular dermis at 30% concentration, enabling deeper pigment targeting
SA produces more uniform whitish frosting, providing a reliable depth endpoint in darker skin
SA is lipophilic with comedolytic activity and self-neutralises, reducing the risk of post-peel PIH in darker skin types
questions.exp: Salicylic acid is a lipophilic beta-hydroxy acid that penetrates sebum-filled follicles (comedolytic), targeting follicular PIH. Crucially, SA self-neutralises — precipitating as a white pseudofrost when it reaches saturation, preventing uncontrolled penetration depth. This makes it significantly safer in Fitzpatrick types IV–VI compared to GA, which can trigger rebound PIH if depth is not precisely controlled. SA does not reach reticular dermis at clinical concentrations.

questions.q: A 35-year-old patient has 1–3mm diameter reticular leg veins unresponsive to sclerotherapy attempts (needle phobia). The MOST appropriate laser modality for these vessels is:
opts: Long-pulsed 1064nm Nd:YAG laser with dynamic cooling
595nm pulsed dye laser (PDL)
532nm KTP laser
810nm diode laser
questions.exp: Long-pulsed 1064nm Nd:YAG is the laser of choice for 1–3mm leg reticular veins: it penetrates 3–5mm (sufficient for deeper leg vessels), and at long pulse durations (20–100ms) selectively coagulates these vessels. PDL (595nm) and KTP (532nm) are effective for smaller facial telangiectasias (<0.5mm) but lack adequate penetration depth for leg reticular veins. Additionally, 1064nm has lower melanin absorption, reducing epidermal damage in tanned skin.

questions.q: Following a medium-depth TCA peel (35%) in a Fitzpatrick type III patient, the recommended duration of strict daily SPF ≥50+ broad-spectrum photoprotection is:
opts: 2 weeks — until complete re-epithelialisation restores the stratum corneum barrier
At least 3–6 months — as new melanocytes remain vulnerable to UV-induced upregulation throughout post-peel recovery
1 month — as the newly formed epidermis reaches full UV tolerance within 30 days
Lifelong photoprotection beginning 1 week post-peel, regardless of original indication
questions.exp: Post medium-depth chemical peel, the new epidermis is thin and functionally immature for several months. UV exposure triggers rapid upregulation of tyrosinase in recovering melanocytes — the major risk factor for post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH), particularly in Fitzpatrick types III–VI. Guidelines uniformly recommend broad-spectrum SPF ≥50+ sunscreen for at least 3–6 months post-procedure, with physical sun avoidance during peak UV hours.

questions.q: Which of the following CORRECTLY matches botulinum toxin serotypes to their SNARE protein cleavage targets?
opts: BoNT-A cleaves VAMP (synaptobrevin); BoNT-B cleaves SNAP-25 at Gln197-Arg198
BoNT-E cleaves syntaxin 1A; BoNT-C cleaves SNAP-25 and VAMP simultaneously
BoNT-A and BoNT-E both cleave SNAP-25 (at different cleavage sites); BoNT-B cleaves VAMP (synaptobrevin)
BoNT-C cleaves VAMP exclusively; BoNT-D and BoNT-G cleave syntaxin at distinct sites
questions.exp: SNARE cleavage specificity: BoNT-A (Botox/Dysport/Xeomin) cleaves SNAP-25 between Gln197–Arg198; BoNT-E also cleaves SNAP-25 but between Arg180–Ile181, removing a longer C-terminal fragment (shorter clinical duration). BoNT-B (Myobloc/Neurobloc) cleaves VAMP (synaptobrevin) at Gln76–Phe77. BoNT-C is unique in cleaving both syntaxin-1 AND SNAP-25. BoNT-D, F, and G all cleave VAMP at different sites than BoNT-B.
